note: Public lands is a cached raster with the six agency colours baked into the PNG, so it cannot be hatched. Stripes need polygons. This asks the surface-management service which sublayers it has and whether any of them will answer a query.

The other way to the same polygons. PAD-US already backs the land-manager lookup in the details panel, so if it will answer a bbox query with Mang_Name the app can draw BLM itself - and the pattern becomes a styling decision rather than a data problem.
The replacement for the 404ing BLM recreation service. If its fields name a site type it can join the USGS points under the same icons.

The atlas viewer names its own tiles: image_tiles/tiles2024/tile_{z}_{x}_{y}.png. This is the calibrated sky-brightness overlay rather than a photograph of streetlights, so it is the better of the two if it draws.
The statewide six-inch mosaic. Answers, but draws nothing over Hardyville where the three-inch does - so it needs a different sublayer or renderer before it is worth offering.
